title: Decisions by industry
subtitle: Manufacturing, healthcare and retail each turn on a different Microsoft product decision. Get it wrong and the implementation cannot fix it.

cards.imageAlt: Manufacturing plant floor, Business Central decision
cards.title: Manufacturing
cards.description: Business Central or Supply Chain Management is settled by your production data model, not your headcount. A run that yields co-products rules Business Central out. Discrete production usually belongs on Business Central Premium, however many plants you run.

cards.title: Healthcare PHI
cards.description: The BAA reaches Teams, Exchange and SharePoint. It does not configure them: audit logs keep 180 days against a years-long lookback.

cards.title: Multi-store retail
cards.description: Most mid-market specialty retailers belong on Business Central rather than Dynamics 365 Commerce. Stock and sales read the same in every store, and you are not paying for a pricing engine you will not run.
